items.title: A September rate HIKE is a coin flip, not a cut
items.detail: August payrolls came in at +162k against a 55k consensus with unemployment steady at 4.1%. The 2-year closed Fri at a fresh 52-week high of 4.374% and the 5-year at 4.545%, also a 52-week high. Market pricing for a September hike sits near 50%. Next week's CPI and PPI decide it. Every high-multiple name in this book is priced off that decision.

items.title: Hormuz throughput has collapsed 77% and Brent is near $95.73
items.detail: Tanker transits through the strait have fallen from 21.6m bpd in Q4 2025 to roughly 4.9m bpd in Q2 2026, with marine war-risk insurance at multi-year highs. Brent rose more than 8% on the week. The EU has now joined the US sanctions campaign and Iran fired at Kuwait on Thursday. This is an inflation input the Fed cannot control and a cost shock for every fuel-intensive business.

items.title: Market leadership is extremely narrow
items.detail: On Friday only three of eleven S&P sectors advanced - Tech (+0.44%), Industrials (+0.22%) and Utilities (+0.12%) - while the index fell 0.38%. The gains that did occur were concentrated in memory and AI semis (MU +6.1%, SNDK +11.9%, ALAB +9.75%). Narrow leadership means the index is vulnerable to a single-theme reversal.

items.title: Single-name earnings risk is producing 17-22% one-day moves
items.detail: On Friday alone Guidewire fell 19.93%, Lululemon 17.38% and Fair Isaac 16.68% - the last on a regulatory directive rather than earnings. Position sizing matters more than usual when a single print or ruling can take a fifth off a large-cap in one session.

items.title: Political pressure on the Fed is now explicit
items.detail: On Friday President Trump publicly demanded the Fed cut rates or he would 'stop trading with countries with which we have a deficit'. Chair Kevin Warsh faces a September decision under open political pressure. Policy uncertainty of this kind widens the distribution of outcomes for every rate-sensitive asset.

items.title: Foreign demand for US Treasuries is being reconsidered
items.detail: Norway's $2.3tn sovereign wealth fund proposed cutting its government-bond benchmark weighting from 70% to 50%, which would mean roughly $80bn less in US Treasuries from its ~$215bn holding. Implementation is years out, but it is a signal about structural demand at the long end, where the 30-year already sits at 5.243%.

items.title: AI capex commitments are becoming fixed costs
items.detail: Constellation's 20-year agreements with Microsoft (835MW) and Meta (1,121MW), and Vistra's 2,609MW with Meta, are contractual obligations that do not flex if AI revenue disappoints. Broadcom has guided FY28 AI revenue to $230bn. The build-out is now committed years ahead of the revenue that has to pay for it.
